context:
A draft README section was copied from Claude Code's Workflow docs into a Codex plugin package. The copied text says:

```md
Use the built-in Workflow tool to launch subagents. The model invokes Workflow directly, and the live workflow tree appears automatically in the Claude Code UI. Every invocation returns a scriptPath. Re-run with the same scriptPath and resumeFromRunId to replay the unchanged prefix for free.
```

The Codex plugin implementation has these facts:

- Users write a plain JavaScript workflow script and run it with `agent-workflows run <script>`.
- The CLI copies the script into `.agent-workflows/runs/<runId>/script.mjs` and writes `status.json`, `result.json`, `journal.json`, and `progress.log`.
- Subagents run through `codex exec`, not an in-session built-in model tool.
- Progress is visible through `agent-workflows watch <runId> --follow` or MCP resources, not an automatic native UI tree.
- Resume is content-addressed by prompt plus result-affecting options. Same script, args, and flags should hit the journal, but independent unchanged calls can still hit even when an earlier independent call changed.
- Package READMEs own public CLI behavior and stable file-format docs.

The team wants docs that are honest enough for users, not a marketing comparison page. The docs should not describe the editing process or say "changed from Claude" in the public target wording.
task: Prepare a public documentation migration plan and replacement wording for porting a Workflow feature from Claude Code docs to a Codex plugin. Preserve semantics without claiming unsupported integration.
title: Workflow Documentation Port to Codex Plugin
